scope: Remaining source-code defects identified after dependency remediation; no deployment or live-service operations
fixed: Backend compilation: Judge Prisma models and additive migration, geocoding validation, Stripe construction and type compatibility; build failures are no longer swallowed.

Production authentication fails closed for missing or invalid Firebase credentials. Demo tokens require explicit backend opt-in in development or test and are disabled in production. HTTP and sockets share revoked-token verification.

Chat, typing and read receipts check active match membership, age, account status and blocks. Receipts update only received messages. Presence is limited to eligible matches and respects activity privacy.
Blocking deactivates matches and removes follows. Passes no longer count as positive likes, produce matches or consume normal daily like quotas.

Public profile and message payloads omit email, Firebase identity, birth date, device tokens, billing IDs and coordinates. Age, location/distance and activity privacy controls are honored; missing distance is not invented.

Profile mutations cannot claim foreign upload URLs. Deletion validates ownership, filename, containment and symlinks. Upload errors clean up newly written media; multipart and image bounds are enforced.
Identity verification no longer self-approves. The UI explains that verification is unavailable until a trusted review workflow exists.
Private and rejected post metadata is filtered from feeds, profiles, replies, saves and reactions. Pagination validates cursors and limits, handles identical timestamps and terminates correctly.
Notification read operations are restricted to the recipient.
Judge approval and cooldown transitions cannot be bypassed through continue, approve, decline or request. Late AI evaluations cannot overwrite cooldowns; concurrent resume votes are handled.
Stripe webhooks validate signatures, return retryable failures when configuration or persistence is unavailable, and preserve subscription identity on pause for later resume.
Frontend API, uploads and sockets share token selection; sockets refresh credentials on reconnect and disconnect on logout. Profile editing preserves canonical media URLs for mutations.
All existing active frontend lint errors and warnings resolved with concrete typing and module separation. Routes are lazy-loaded.
Container startup applies tracked migrations and fails on errors; it no longer uses db push --accept-data-loss. Docker context excludes credentials, uploads and generated files.

browser.scope: Public routes, redirects and horizontal overflow; external requests blocked

databaseTests.database: Isolated temporary PostgreSQL 17.5 on localhost; no application database used

backend.stripeModuleCompatibility: Compiled CommonJS and Vitest ESM both passed; signed fixture webhooks use the real Stripe signature implementation without external requests

validation.dependencyAudit: No dependency versions changed in this remediation. Previous full frontend and backend audits both had zero findings; see dependency-remediation-2026-11-21.json.

requiredSteps: Back up the target database and check its migration history; baseline existing schemas if previously managed with db push. Apply tracked migrations with prisma migrate deploy before serving this build.
Supply production Firebase and billing secrets through deployment configuration. Local backend demo mode requires NODE_ENV=development, DEMO_AUTH_ENABLED=true and absent Firebase credentials.
For integration tests, explicitly set TEST_DATABASE_URL to a disposable localhost database with test in its name; the suite intentionally refuses implicit application-database access.

remainingReleaseWork: Live Firebase sign-in/revocation, push delivery, Stripe test-mode checkout and deployed media persistence still need staging credentials and validation. No provider accounts or charges were used here.

Uploads are still served as static URLs. Metadata privacy and deletion ownership are fixed, but access-controlled private media delivery, storage retention and multi-instance persistence require a separate storage implementation before treating media as confidential.

Identity verification and content moderation still need trusted operational workflows. Existing badges and historical pass/like records need data review: prior passes were indistinguishable from positive likes, and prior verification was self-approved.
No container image build was run because the local Docker daemon was unavailable. The existing Vite environment file still produces a nonfatal NODE_ENV warning.
